newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-OFF-SPINNER CHAUHAN CLEARED FOR SELECTION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-OFF-SPINNER CHAUHAN CLEARED FOR SELECTION.

text.p: Indian cricket chiefs on Tuesday lifted their two-year international ban on off-spinner Rajesh Chauhan who was suspected of throwing by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
India's Cricket Control Board said it had cleared Chauhan for selection for his country while authorities continued to scrutinise his technique.

"The BCCI decided it was not fair to compel Chauhan to remain under the cloud of a suspect action till complete footage was made available (for scrutiny)," said BCCI's outgoing secretary Jagmohan Dalmiya, the new ICC president.
Chauhan played 15 tests and 22 one-day internationals before being sidelined from selection after the home series against New Zealand in 1995. But he has never been called for throwing.

He has continued to perform exceptionally well in domestic competitions and was leading wicket-taker with 55 victims last season. He is now available for selection for next month's Asia Cup in Sri Lanka.
Chauhan's selection for international matches was put on hold by the Indian board after the ICC raised doubts about his bowling action in 1995.
The BCCI formed a two-member committee comprising former Indian captain Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev to observe Chauhan's action and also study the video footage sent by the ICC.
Dev, a member of the ICC committee to review suspect bowling actions, and Gavaskar found the footage was incomplete since it did not show the complete shoulder movement and rotation of the arm.
Gavaskar and Dev had a close look at Chauhan's action by making him bowl in the nets in New Delhi last month but ruled that it should be scrutinised in actual match situations.
"He has a bent-arm action and that's why we are here," Dev said while studying Chauhan's action in May.
The BCCI has asked the ICC to furnish additional footage and has passed on the views of Gavaskar and Dev.
